Report the calibration of predicted observation probabilities

Source: R/margot_lmtp_observation_report.R
margot_lmtp_observation_report.Rd

margot_lmtp_observation_report() summarises, for each wave, how well predicted probabilities of remaining observed describe who was in fact observed among the records that reached that wave. Each column of the three matrices is one wave and each row one participant. For wave \(j\), let \(R_j\) be the records with reached[, j] true, \(y_i\) the indicator observed[i, j] and \(p_i\) the predicted probability probability[i, j]. The report gives the number reached, the number that continued (\(\sum_{i \in R_j} y_i\)), the Brier score \(|R_j|^{-1} \sum_{i \in R_j} (p_i - y_i)^2\) and the log loss \(|R_j|^{-1} \sum_{i \in R_j} -\{y_i \log p_i + (1 - y_i) \log(1 - p_i)\}\), computed as mean(-ifelse(y == 1, log(p), log1p(-p))). Records that did not reach a wave do not enter it.

Usage

margot_lmtp_observation_report(
  reached,
  observed,
  probability,
  wave_labels = NULL
)

Arguments

reached

Logical matrix, one row per participant and one column per wave, true where a record reached that wave and was at risk of being lost to observation. Missing values are not allowed.

observed

Logical matrix of the same dimensions, true where a record that reached the wave remained observed. It must be non-missing wherever reached is true and may not be true where reached is false; its values elsewhere are ignored. Convert a 0/1 censoring indicator with observed == 1.

probability

Numeric matrix of the same dimensions holding the predicted probability of remaining observed. It must lie between 0 and 1 inclusive and be non-missing wherever reached is true; its values elsewhere are ignored.

wave_labels

Optional labels, one per column. Column names of reached are used when available, then Wave 1, Wave 2, and so on.

Value

A data frame of class margot_lmtp_observation_report with one row per wave and columns wave, reached, continued, brier, log_loss and n_infinite_log_loss. It contains no participant-level values.

Details

Probabilities are not clipped. A probability of exactly 0 or 1 is valid: when it matches the observed indicator the record contributes 0 to the log loss, and when it contradicts it (a record observed with predicted probability 0, or not observed with predicted probability 1) the record's loss, and so the wave's log loss, is Inf. The column n_infinite_log_loss counts those records, so an infinite log loss can be traced to a confident wrong prediction rather than mistaken for a numerical failure. A wave that no record reached has zero counts and NA scores.

The report describes the observation model; it is descriptive and attaches no positivity or estimator-stability judgement. Weight concentration is reported separately by margot_lmtp_analysis_weight_report().

See also

margot_lmtp_analysis_weight_report(), margot_lmtp_censoring_report()

Examples

reached <- cbind(rep(TRUE, 6), c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE))
probability <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.9, 0.5, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), ncol = 2)
observed <- cbind(reached[, 2], c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE))
margot_lmtp_observation_report(reached, observed, probability, wave_labels = c("2019", "2020"))
#>   wave reached continued     brier  log_loss n_infinite_log_loss
#> 1 2019       6         4 0.1266667 0.3999962                   0
#> 2 2020       4         3 0.1750000 0.5108256                   0
